newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Tuesday due to continuous profit-taking on concerns about possible sharp rises in stockpiles data to be announced tonight by the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 20,900 yuan ($2,518) per tonne, losing 350 yuan. It opened at 21,050 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 21,160 and a low of 20,890.
January fell 110 to 20,480, February 180 to 20,550, March 300 to 20,720, May 360 to 20,950 and June 300 to 21,000.
Combined volume rose to 55,150 tonnes from 50,600.

Copper opened lower and stayed around the opening level in the morning session. But then heavy profit-taking pushed prices sharply down during the rest of session triggered by expecations of rises in LME stockpiles, traders said.
"Profit-taking by long position holders dominated today's trading on expectations of LME stockpile rumours," a trader said. "They have gained a lot over the past few days."
"All later-maturing contracts fell below the key 21,000 yuan support level which seriously hurt the confidence of long position holders," he added.
Analysts said 21,000 yuan would be a strong resistance level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended up. January rose 50 to 14,000 yuan per tonne, February 90 to 14,290 and March 350 to 14,800.
Combined volume rose to 1,820 tonnes from 790.
